les: Nie alles wat jy koop, kan jy vashou nie

items.bewering: 'n Brood uit die winkel kan jy vashou. 'n Haarsny kan jy nie vashou nie. Jy betaal die haarkapper vir die werk en nie vir 'n ding nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Service (economics)': services are intangible acts or performances, not manufactured, transported or stocked; the article uses the hairdresser's chair as its example. BITRE (Australian Government) staff paper 'What are services and who provides them' notes that a service can leave a tangible result yet the service itself is a performance, not a good. Check of the mapping: the contrast bread = a thing you own and hold, haircut = paid-for work, is the standard goods/services contrast. A learner who says 'but I can touch my cut hair' is touching the result, not what was bought; the next sentence ('vir die werk en nie vir 'n ding nie') says what was paid for, so the mapping holds.

items.bewering: 'n Diens is werk wat iemand vir 'n ander doen.
items.bron: Holds in its context, and only there: the sentence before it ('Jy betaal die haarkapper vir die werk en nie vir 'n ding nie') supplies the 'no thing changes hands' criterion that every source treats as what defines a service (Wikipedia 'Service (economics)'; Black's-style legal dictionary entry 'useful labor that does not produce a tangible commodity'). The same sentence standing alone as a glossary entry is reported separately below.

items.bewering: Die haarkapper se werk is verby sodra die laaste hare gesny is. 'n Diens kan jy nie vir later bêre nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Service (economics)': services 'are produced and consumed simultaneously' and 'one cannot store services for future use' (perishability); the same point appears in the goods-vs-services overviews of INFLIBNET e-PG Pathshala 'Goods Vs. Service Marketing' (the unsold-airline-seat example). The first sentence is a fair description of a haircut service as a time-bound performance.

items.bewering: Die haarkapper verkoop nie die skêr nie, maar die vaardigheid om hare te sny.
items.blok: Die vaardigheid bly by die mens
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Service (economics)' (provider adds value through an act or performance; ownership of no object passes); Wiktionary 'skill' (capacity to do something well). The tools stay with the hairdresser; what the customer pays for is skilled work.

items.bewering: 'n Vaardigheid is die vermoë om iets goed te doen. 'n Mens kry dit deur te leer of deur te oefen.
items.blok: Die vaardigheid bly by die mens
items.bron: Wiktionary 'skill', sense 1: 'A capacity to do something well', usually gained through learning rather than innate talent. Britannica Dictionary 'skill' (as quoted in search results; the page itself returned 403): the ability to do something that comes from training, experience or practice. Dutch cognate 'vaardigheid' carries the same sense (DBNL, historical Dutch dictionary). The WAT volume for V is not available online to check the Afrikaans entry directly, but the cognate and the English sources agree.

items.bewering: Die haarkapper bied hierdie vaardigheid vir ander mense aan. Die vaardigheid bly by die haarkapper nadat jou haarsny klaar is. Die diens is die werk wat met die vaardigheid gedoen is.
items.blok: Die vaardigheid bly by die mens
items.bron: Follows from the definitions confirmed above (Wiktionary 'skill': a capacity, i.e. something the person has; Wikipedia 'Service (economics)': a service is the act performed). A capacity is not used up or transferred by being used for one customer.

items.bewering: In baie dorpe en op baie plase werk mense wat dienste verkoop.
items.bron: Stats SA Quarterly Labour Force Survey (as summarised by Codera's QLFS analysis): community and social services and wholesale/retail trade are the largest employers in South Africa; agriculture employs roughly 0.94 million people (QLFS 2026 Q2 via Economy.com aggregator). Under the lesson's own definition, work done for others for pay on farms qualifies. A general claim, and not false.

items.bewering: 'n Dokter help jou om gesond te word en 'n onderwyser leer jou lees. 'n Loodgieter maak 'n lekkende pyp reg en 'n taxibestuurder ry jou skool toe.
items.bron: Plumber: dictionary definitions (Vocabulary.com, Dictionary.com via search) 'a person who installs and repairs piping, fixtures ... in connection with the water supply, drainage systems', with fixing leaks named as everyday work. Taxi to school is South African practice: Stats SA National Household Travel Survey 2013 (P0320) puts about 14.8% of learners travelling to school by taxi, 22.4% in Gauteng; NHTS 2020 (statssa.gov.za/?p=14054) shows taxi as the second most-used mode nationally. Doctor and teacher descriptions are uncontroversial occupational descriptions.

items.bewering: Net soos die haarkapper verkoop al vier hulle vaardigheid.
items.bron: Count checked: four workers are named (dokter, onderwyser, loodgieter, taxibestuurder), so 'al vier' is correct. Mapping checked: each is paid for skilled work done for someone else, with no object passing to the customer, exactly as with the hairdresser (Wikipedia 'Service (economics)'; Wikipedia 'Trade in services', which lists health, education and transport among service sectors). A learner extending the comparison to these four does not go astray. That many of them are employees, such as a public-school teacher or a driver working for a taxi owner, does not break it at this level: they still sell their skilled work, to an employer.

items.bewering: Vaardighede en dienste word ook oor 'n landsgrens verkoop.
items.blok: Dienste wat oor 'n grens verkoop word
items.bron: WTO General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS), four modes of supply, summarised in Wikipedia 'Trade in services', the US International Trade Administration 'Trade Guide: WTO GATS' and the SADC TIS paper 'The GATS and the new MSITS 2010'. Trade in services across borders is a recognised category of international trade.

items.bewering: 'n Besoeker uit 'n ander land betaal hier vir slaapplek en vir 'n ete wat 'n restaurant kook en bedien. Suid-Afrika verkoop 'n diens sonder dat 'n vrag die land verlaat.
items.blok: Dienste wat oor 'n grens verkoop word
items.bron: South African Reserve Bank, Quarterly Bulletin September 2015, Box 4 'Tourist spending in South Africa': 'Spending by tourists in South Africa accounts for almost 95 per cent of the "travel receipts" item, the largest revenue component in the services account of South Africa's balance of payments.' IMF BPM6 para 10.86 (as cited in IMF and World Bank metadata): travel credits are goods and services acquired from an economy by non-residents during visits there; Eurostat's travel presentation to a UN workshop lists accommodation and food and beverages as the most common items. GATS Mode 2 'consumption abroad', where the WTO's own example is a foreign tourist staying in a hotel. The restaurant meal is counted in the services account, so the claim holds as stated.

items.bewering: Toerisme is wanneer mense vir 'n kort tyd reis na 'n plek buite hulle gewone lewe: nie waar hulle woon, werk of skool gaan nie.
items.blok: Dienste wat oor 'n grens verkoop word
items.bron: UN/UNWTO International Recommendations for Tourism Statistics 2008, as presented in UNWTO 'Basic concepts and definitions' (unstats.un.org, Vientiane workshop) and Statistics Canada 'TSA Concepts and Definitions': a visitor travels to a main destination outside his or her usual environment for less than a year. The 'usual environment' is where a person carries out regular life routines, and it excludes regular commuting between home and the place of work or study. 'Kort tyd' is a fair simplification of 'less than a year', and 'nie waar hulle woon, werk of skool gaan nie' matches the usual-environment exclusion.

items.bewering: 'n Diens is werk wat iemand vir 'n ander doen.
items.bron: Read alone, this definition leaves out the criterion that makes something a service, and so includes work that produces a good. A baker baking bread for a customer, or a carpenter making a table for someone, does work for another, yet sells a good, which is the very contrast this lesson opens with. Sources define a service by that missing criterion: Wikipedia 'Service (economics)' (intangible acts; not manufactured, transported or stocked); legal and economic dictionary sense 'useful labor that does not produce a tangible commodity' (Black's-style entry; Taxguru compilation: 'does not result in ownership' of a physical good). In study block 'Jy betaal vir die werk' the preceding sentence supplies the criterion; the glossary entry has nothing beside it.
items.regstelling: Put the missing criterion into the glossary entry itself, so that it reads alone as work done for someone where the buyer is paying for the work and does not receive a thing to keep or hold. Example of the sense required, not prescribed wording: "'n Diens is werk wat iemand vir 'n ander doen, waarvoor jy betaal sonder om 'n ding te kry wat jy kan hou." Check that the study-block sentence and the glossary entry stay consistent with each other after the change.

items.bewering: Die vermoë om iets goed te doen, wat 'n mens deur leer of oefening kry.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'skill', sense 1 ('A capacity to do something well', usually gained through learning rather than innate talent); Britannica Dictionary 'skill' as quoted in search results (ability coming from training, experience or practice). Read alone, it is accurate.

items.bewering: Toerisme is wanneer mense vir 'n kort tyd reis na 'n plek buite hulle gewone lewe: nie waar hulle woon, werk of skool gaan nie. Toeriste betaal dikwels daar vir slaapplek en vir etes in restaurante.
items.bron: UNWTO/IRTS 2008 usual-environment definition, as above (unstats.un.org UNWTO 'Basic concepts and definitions'; Statistics Canada TSA concepts). Eurostat 'Agenda item 8 - Travel' (UN trade-statistics workshop, Amman 2012) lists accommodation and food and beverages as the most common items visitors buy. 'Dikwels' is the right hedge: day visitors and people staying with friends or relatives do not pay for accommodation.

opsomming: One fault: the glossary entry for 'diens', read on its own, would also cover a baker or carpenter making a good for someone, so it fails at exactly the goods-versus-services line this lesson teaches and needs the 'no thing to keep' criterion added; every other claim checked out, the lesson contains no superlatives, and both comparisons (bread versus haircut, and 'net soos die haarkapper') hold when a learner reasons further with them.
